= GitHub Actions

This file describes the GitHub Actions workflows in `.github/workflows/`
as they run today.
It does not change those workflows.
The section outline is the same shape for each repository,
so two copies can be diffed and then converged.

A Claude mention is the maintainer text that asks Claude to run.
The Codex review trigger comment is the maintainer comment that asks Codex to review.
The workflow files match those literal handles.
This file does not repeat the handles.

== Overview

=== From a pull request to a release

. Any pull request, and any push to `main` or to a `vX.Y.x` branch,
  runs Continuous Integration:
  `npm ci`, `npm run lint:build`, and `npm run dist`
  on Node `22.x`, `24.x`, and `26.x`.
. Renovate (`renovate.json`) opens one pull request per dependency.
  Dependency Review runs when Renovate opens, reopens, or updates that pull request,
  and when a maintainer adds the `claude-review` label.
  Claude reviews it with the `update-dependency` skill
  and may push one signed follow-up commit.
. Codex (the `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` GitHub App) reviews Renovate pull requests
  and pull requests that Claude opened for an issue.
  The workflows do not post the Codex review trigger comment.
  Codex Review reads Codex's summary comment.
  While findings are still open, it asks Claude to fix them on the first two reviewed rounds.
  The third round is reported and not fixed.
  A successful Dependency Review run starts that loop again.
  Codex Review Watchdog flags a loop pull request whose head has had no Codex review for two hours.
. A Claude mention from a maintainer, or the `claude` label on an issue that is not a release,
  runs the Claude workflow.
  For an issue, Claude opens `claude-issue-<number>-...` from `main` and opens a pull request
  that is ready for review, so Codex reviews it.
  A later Claude mention on that pull request continues the same branch.
  A later mention on the issue does not.
. A release starts as an open issue titled `Release @perfective/build vX.Y.Z`.
  Adding the `claude` label runs Publish PR and does not run the general Claude workflow.
  Publish PR sets the version, runs `npm update`,
  and has Claude write `CHANGELOG.adoc`, sync the READMEs, and update `ROADMAP.adoc`,
  then open a `Publish vX.Y.Z` pull request from `publish-vX.Y.Z`.
  Re-adding the label, or a Claude mention from a maintainer on that pull request,
  continues the same branch.
  The Codex loop does not include Publish pull requests.
. The maintainer squash-merges the Publish pull request after Continuous Integration passes,
  then signs and pushes an annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag.
. Publish runs on that tag.
  It checks the signature, that the commit is on `main` or `vX.Y.x`,
  that `package.json` matches the tag, and that `CHANGELOG.adoc` has the version section.
  It then runs `lint:build` and `dist` on Node `26.x`
  and runs `npm publish --provenance ./dist`.
  The maintainer creates the GitHub Release manually.
  This workflow does not.

=== What each workflow owns

[cols="2,3"]
|===
|File |Owns

|`ci.yaml`
|Lint and build on pull requests, `main`, and backport branches

|`dependency-review.yaml`
|Claude's review of a Renovate pull request

|`claude.yaml`
|A Claude mention or the `claude` label, outside a release

|`codex-review.yaml`
|The fix loop after Codex reviews a Renovate or issue pull request

|`codex-watchdog.yaml`
|An hourly flag when that review has not arrived

|`publish-pr.yaml`
|The Publish pull request for a release issue

|`publish.yaml`
|npm publish from a signed `v*` tag
|===

== Shared conventions

=== Runners

Every job uses `ubuntu-latest`.

=== Action pins

Pins are major tags, not commit SHAs.

[cols="2,1"]
|===
|Action |Pin

|`actions/checkout`
|`v7`

|`actions/setup-node`
|`v7`

|`anthropics/claude-code-action`
|`v1`
|===

Claude jobs pass `--model claude-opus-5-5`.

=== Node.js

There is no `.nvmrc`, no `.node-version`, and no `engines` field in `package.json`.
Each job passes `node-version` to `actions/setup-node`.

* Continuous Integration uses a matrix: `22.x`, `24.x`, and `26.x`.
* Every other job that installs dependencies uses `26.x`.

=== Secrets

Claude jobs need the repository secret `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
Shell steps that call `gh` use `github.token` (the automatic `GITHUB_TOKEN`), not a personal token.
Publish authenticates to npm with GitHub OIDC (`id-token: write`).
There is no `NPM_TOKEN` secret.
No workflow reads any other secret.

=== Permissions

`publish.yaml` and `publish-pr.yaml` set workflow `permissions` to `{}`,
so a job has only the permissions it declares.
The other workflows leave the workflow permissions unset
and declare permissions on each job.
`ci.yaml` declares none: it uses the repository default for `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

`id-token: write` on a Claude job is how the action gets a GitHub App token.
Pushes made with that token start Continuous Integration.
Pushes made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not.

=== Concurrency

Groups that must not cancel a waiting run set `cancel-in-progress: false` and `queue: max`
(up to 100 waiting runs, in the order they started waiting).
The Claude writer jobs share `claude-<number>`:
the issue number for an issue and for the pull request Claude opened for it,
and the pull request number otherwise.
One writer at a time pushes to that branch.

=== Labels

* `claude` starts the Claude workflow on an issue, or Publish PR on a release issue.
* `release` on an issue keeps the general Claude workflow from starting.
* `claude-review` reruns Dependency Review on a Renovate pull request.
* `dependencies` is Renovate's pull-request label.
  Vulnerability alerts also get `vulnerability`.
* `help wanted` marks a pull request that is waiting on a maintainer.
  Renovate adds it for a major update, a peer dependency update, and a TypeScript update.
  Claude adds it for **NEEDS HUMAN**.
  The watchdog adds it when a loop pull request has no Codex review.
* `renovate-regenerate` is Renovate's rebase checkbox.
  Renovate recreates the branch and drops follow-up commits.

=== Mentions

A job runs on a Claude mention only when `author_association` is
`OWNER`, `MEMBER`, or `COLLABORATOR`.
The `claude` label path does not repeat that check in the workflow;
the action checks write access again.
Workflows do not post the Codex review trigger comment.

=== Install failures

Where a Claude job runs `npm ci || npm install`,
a failure of both commands does not stop the job.
The prompt tells Claude to report **NEEDS HUMAN**,
and the commit tools are turned off for that run.
Claude must not use `--force` or `--legacy-peer-deps`.

=== Commits Claude pushes

`main` requires signed commits.
Claude commits through the GitHub API (`use_commit_signing: true`).
The jobs disallow `git commit`, `git push`, `git merge`, `git rebase`, and `git pull`.

== Workflows

=== ci.yaml

==== Name

Continuous Integration.

==== Triggers

* `push` to `main` and to branches matching `v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.x`.
* `pull_request` against any branch (`**`).
  The activity types are the GitHub default: `opened`, `synchronize`, and `reopened`.

No path filter, label filter, or mention condition.
No `workflow_dispatch`.

==== Permissions

No `permissions` key.
The job uses the repository default for `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
The steps do not call the GitHub API.

==== Secrets

None.

==== Node.js

Matrix `node-version`: `22.x`, `24.x`, `26.x`,
passed to `actions/setup-node`.

==== Actions

`actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`.

==== Concurrency

None.

==== Jobs

===== build

Display name: Build.
One job per matrix entry.
No timeout.

. Check out the default ref for the event.
. Set up that matrix Node version.
. `npm ci`.
. `npm run lint:build` (Prettier check).
. `npm run dist` (the default Gulp task).

There is no test step.
This package has no tests.

==== Place in the flow

This is the check that runs on pull requests and on pushes to `main` and backport branches.
Publish repeats `lint:build` and `dist` on Node `26.x` before it publishes.
It does not call this workflow.

=== dependency-review.yaml

==== Name

Dependency Review.

==== Triggers

`pull_request` types `opened`, `reopened`, `synchronize`, and `labeled`.
No branch filter and no path filter.

The `review` job runs only when the pull request author is `renovate[bot]`, and either:

* the event is `labeled` and the label is `claude-review`, or
* the event is not `labeled` and `github.event.sender` is `renovate[bot]`.

A follow-up push from Claude does not start another review.
A label other than `claude-review` starts a workflow run whose job is skipped.
Concurrency is on the job, so that skipped run does not cancel a review that is in progress.

==== Permissions

Job `review`:

* `contents: write` to push the follow-up commit
* `pull-requests: write` to post the report
* `issues: write` to update the tracking comment and labels
* `id-token: write` for the Claude GitHub App token
* `actions: read` to read the pull request's Continuous Integration results

==== Secrets

`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.

==== Node.js

`26.x` via `actions/setup-node@v7`.

==== Actions

`actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`.

==== Concurrency

Group `dependency-review-<pull request number>`, `cancel-in-progress: true`.
A newer Renovate update cancels the review that is running.
No `queue` setting.

==== Jobs

===== review

Display name: Review the dependency update.
Timeout 60 minutes.

. Check out the pull request head branch, `fetch-depth: 0`.
. Set up Node `26.x`.
. `npm ci`, or `npm install` when `npm ci` fails.
  Both failing leaves the commit tools off and continues.
. Run Claude in tag mode (`track_progress: true`):
  a tracking comment holds the report,
  and the action allows the signed-commit tool, so `claude_args` does not list it.
  `allowed_bots` is `renovate[bot]`.
  `restrict_untrusted_prs` is `false`.
  `use_commit_signing` is `true`.
  The prompt runs `.agents/skills/update-dependency/SKILL.md`
  and tells Claude not to post a Codex mention.
  Codex reviews the branch on its own when commits are pushed.
. Fail the job when the action did not run Claude
  (`conclusion` output empty, and the step itself did not fail).
  The job comments on the pull request, adds `help wanted`, and exits non-zero.
  The comment tells a maintainer to tick the rebase checkbox
  when the log says workflow validation failed
  (the pull request is based on an older `main`).
  A failed Claude step fails the job without that comment.

Allowed tools, plus the signed-commit tool the action adds in tag mode:

* `Read`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep`
* `Bash(npm install)`, `Bash(npm outdated)`, `Bash(npm ls:*)`, `Bash(npm view:*)`
* `Bash(npm run lint)`, `Bash(npm run lint:build)`, `Bash(npm run dist)`
* `Bash(git status)`, `Bash(git log:*)`, `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git show:*)`
* `Bash(gh pr view:*)`, `Bash(gh pr diff:*)`, `Bash(gh pr list:*)`
* `Bash(gh pr edit * --add-label *)`, `Bash(gh pr edit * --remove-label *)`
* `Bash(gh release list:*)`, `Bash(gh release view:*)`
* `Bash(gh api repos/*/compare/*)`, `Bash(gh api repos/*/releases*)`, `Bash(gh api repos/*/contents/*)`
* `WebFetch` for `github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `www.npmjs.com`,
  `www.typescriptlang.org`, `babeljs.io`, `gulpjs.com`, `prettier.io`, and `jestjs.io`

Disallowed tools: `git merge`, `git rebase`, `git pull`, `git commit`, and `git push`.
On an install failure the commit-file and delete-file tools are disallowed as well.

==== Place in the flow

This is the agent review of a Renovate pull request.
When the job succeeds, Codex Review starts again from `workflow_run`
and reads the latest Codex summary, with or without a new commit.
The loop does not start while this job is still running,
and it does not start from a failed or cancelled run.
A pull request that is behind `main` is recreated with `renovate-regenerate`,
not by merging `main` in this job.

=== claude.yaml

==== Name

Claude.

==== Triggers

* `issues`: `opened`, `assigned`, and `labeled`
* `issue_comment`: `created`
* `pull_request_review_comment`: `created`
* `pull_request_review`: `submitted`

No branch filter and no path filter.

The `resolve` job's `if` is the real filter.
Release issues and Publish pull requests are left to `publish-pr.yaml`.

An issue event runs only when the issue is not labeled `release`,
the title does not start with `Release @perfective/build v`,
and either:

* the action is `labeled` and the label is `claude`, or
* the issue body contains a Claude mention and the issue author is a maintainer.

`assigned` has no rule of its own.
An assigned issue runs only when the body mention rule above matches.

An issue comment runs only when the issue is not labeled `release`,
the title does not start with `Release @perfective/build v`,
the comment is not on a pull request titled `Publish v...`,
the comment contains a Claude mention,
and the comment author is a maintainer.

A pull request review comment or review runs only when the head is not a
`publish-v` branch in this repository,
the comment or review body contains a Claude mention,
and the author is a maintainer.

==== Permissions

Job `resolve`: `pull-requests: read`.

Job `claude`:

* `contents: write` to push the work branch
* `pull-requests: write` to open and update the pull request
* `issues: write` to update the tracking comment
* `id-token: write` for the Claude GitHub App token
* `actions: read` to read the pull request's checks

Job `threads`:

* `contents: read` to compare the commits Claude pushed
* `pull-requests: write` to resolve threads

==== Secrets

`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` on the Claude step.
`resolve` and `threads` use `github.token` only.

==== Node.js

Job `claude` uses `26.x` via `actions/setup-node@v7`.
The other jobs do not install Node.

==== Actions

`actions/checkout@v7` and `actions/setup-node@v7` on `claude`.
`anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` on `claude`.
`resolve` and `threads` are shell and `gh` only.

==== Concurrency

`claude` and `threads` use group `claude-<lock>` from `resolve`,
`cancel-in-progress: false`, and `queue: max`.
`resolve` has no concurrency group.
The lock is the issue number when the pull request is one Claude opened for an issue
(`claude-issue-<number>-...` in this repository).
Otherwise it is the issue or pull request number of the event.
Codex Review uses the same group, so the two workflows do not push at the same time.

==== Jobs

===== resolve

Display name: Find the work to lock.
Timeout 5 minutes.
Runs in `runner.temp` so it does not use a checkout of the repository.

Outputs: `lock`, `claude-args`, `claude-pr`, `branch`.

On a pull request, if the author is `claude[bot]`, the head repository is this one,
and the branch matches `claude-issue-<number>-`,
the lock is that issue number and `claude-pr` is the pull request number.

On an issue that already has an open pull request from such a branch,
`claude-args` disallows the commit and delete tools
and appends a system prompt:
Claude answers on the issue, does not commit,
and asks the maintainer to repeat the request as a Claude mention on that pull request.
The action checks out `main` for an issue, so it cannot commit to the existing pull request branch.

===== claude

Display name: Work on the issue or PR.
Needs `resolve`.
Timeout 60 minutes.

. Check out the repository with `fetch-depth: 0`.
  A Renovate author checks out the pull request head,
  so the install matches that lockfile.
  Every other author checks out the default branch.
  Pull request code from other authors does not run before the action.
. Set up Node `26.x`.
. `npm ci`, or `npm install` when `npm ci` fails.
  Both failing leaves the commit tools off and continues.
. When `claude-pr` is set, record the branch head.
  Commits from this run are the ones after that SHA.
. Run Claude.
  `label_trigger` is `claude`.
  `branch_prefix` is `claude-`
  (`claude/...` cannot coexist with a branch named `claude`).
  `use_commit_signing` is `true`.
  `restrict_untrusted_prs` is `false` for `renovate[bot]`
  and for a pull request recorded in `claude-pr`.
  It stays `true` for everyone else, so outside contributors cannot run npm through the action.
  Extra `claude_args` from `resolve` and from a failed install are appended.
. Fail the job when the action did not run Claude.
  The job comments on the issue or pull request and exits non-zero.
  It does not add `help wanted`.
  The comment points at a workflow-files mismatch with `main`, or at the first failed step.
. Mark a draft issue pull request ready with `gh pr ready`,
  including when the Claude step did not succeed.
  Codex does not review drafts.
  When this run pushed commits onto an existing issue pull request,
  pass the pull request number and the before and after SHAs to `threads`.

Allowed tools:

* `Bash(npm install)`, `Bash(npm outdated)`, `Bash(npm ls:*)`, `Bash(npm view:*)`
* `Bash(npm run lint)`, `Bash(npm run lint:build)`, `Bash(npm run dist)`
* `Bash(git status)`, `Bash(git log:*)`, `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git show:*)`
* `Bash(gh issue view:*)`, `Bash(gh pr view:*)`, `Bash(gh pr diff:*)`, `Bash(gh pr list:*)`
* `Bash(gh pr edit * --add-label *)`, `Bash(gh pr edit * --remove-label *)`
* `Bash(gh pr create:*)`, `Bash(gh release view:*)`
* `Bash(gh api repos/*/pulls/*/comments*)`, `Bash(gh api repos/*/pulls/*/reviews*)`
* `WebFetch` for `github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `www.npmjs.com`,
  `www.typescriptlang.org`, `babeljs.io`, `gulpjs.com`, `prettier.io`, and `jestjs.io`

Disallowed tools: `git merge`, `git rebase`, `git pull`, `git commit`, and `git push`.
The commit and delete tools are also disallowed when the issue already has an open Claude pull request,
or when the install failed.

===== threads

Display name: Resolve the threads Claude fixed.
Needs `resolve` and `claude`.
Runs only when `claude` recorded an issue pull request that received new commits.
Timeout 5 minutes.
The step is `continue-on-error: true`.

The job resolves an open review thread when all of these hold:

* the first comment is from `chatgpt-codex-connector` (a `[bot]` suffix is ignored)
* the last comment is from `claude`
* the last comment does not contain **NEEDS HUMAN**
* the last comment contains the full SHA of a commit in the before...after range

The job reads at most 100 threads.
It does not post comments.

==== Place in the flow

This is the path for issue and pull request work that is not a release.
On a Renovate pull request the same workflow can run when a maintainer writes a Claude mention,
with npm allowed and the pull request head checked out.
Dependency Review is the path that runs without that mention.
After this workflow opens an issue pull request, Codex reviews it on its own.
`threads` only resolves threads for a follow-up on a pull request that already existed.

=== codex-review.yaml

==== Name

Codex Review.

==== Triggers

* `issue_comment`: `created` and `edited`
* `workflow_run` of Dependency Review, type `completed`

`issue_comment` and `workflow_run` both run from the default branch.
The loop starts only after this file is on `main`.

The `route-key` job runs when either:

* the comment is on a pull request,
  the pull request author is `renovate[bot]` or `claude[bot]`,
  the comment author is `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`,
  and the body contains `codex-review-state:v1`, or
* the completed Dependency Review run was for `pull_request`,
  its conclusion is `success`,
  and its head repository is this repository.

The condition is on the job, not the workflow,
so a skipped run does not cancel a route that is waiting.

==== Permissions

Job `route-key`: `pull-requests: read`.

Job `route`:

* `contents: read`
* `pull-requests: read`
* `issues: read`
* `actions: read` to list Dependency Review runs

Job `report`:

* `pull-requests: write`
* `issues: write` for the `help wanted` label

Job `fix`:

* `contents: write` to push the follow-up commit
* `pull-requests: write` to reply, resolve threads, and comment
* `issues: write` for the `help wanted` label
* `id-token: write` for the Claude GitHub App token
* `actions: read` to read the pull request's checks

==== Secrets

`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` on the Claude step in `fix`.
The other jobs use `github.token` only.

==== Node.js

Job `fix` uses `26.x` via `actions/setup-node@v7`
when the reviewed commit is still the branch tip.
The other jobs do not install Node.

==== Actions

`actions/checkout@v7` and `actions/setup-node@v7` on `fix`.
`anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` on `fix`.
The other jobs are shell, `gh`, and `gh api graphql`.

==== Concurrency

`route` uses group `codex-review-route-<pull request number>`,
`cancel-in-progress: false`, and `queue: max`.
A later summary edit waits.
Cancelling the route that is running would drop a review
that the next edit would treat as already handled.
A `workflow_run` payload with no pull request number looks the number up from the branch,
so it joins the same group.
When no number can be resolved, the group is `codex-review-route-none` and `route` does not run.

`report` and `fix` use group `claude-<lock>`,
`cancel-in-progress: false`, and `queue: max`.
The lock is the issue number parsed from `claude-issue-<number>-`,
or the pull request number for a Renovate pull request.
That is the same group as `claude.yaml`.

==== Jobs

===== route-key

Display name: Name the route.
Timeout 5 minutes.
Writes the concurrency group and the pull request number.
For `workflow_run`, the number is the first pull request on the payload,
or the open pull request whose head is `owner:branch`.

===== route

Display name: Decide whether Claude should respond.
Needs `route-key`.
Runs when that job succeeded and the group is not `codex-review-route-none`.
Timeout 10 minutes.

Outputs: `action`, `pr`, `branch`, `sha`, `round`, `status`, `kind`, `issue`, `lock`, `comment`.

For `workflow_run`, the job loads the latest Codex summary on the pull request
(`chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` and `codex-review-state:v1`).
There is no previous body, so the result is never treated as already handled.
No summary yet yields `action=skip`.

The hidden state line is a JSON object with `code_review` and `security_review`.
The job acts once per finished review.
A later edit that only resolves threads does not start another round.
A security review that starts or finishes on the same commit does.

`kind` is `dependency` for `renovate[bot]`.
`kind` is `issue` for `claude[bot]` when the head repository is this one
and the branch matches `claude-issue-<number>-`.
Anything else, including a Publish pull request, is skipped.
A closed pull request is skipped.

The code-review outcome is one of:

* `absent` or `pending`: skip
* `invalid` (completed, but neither findings flag is a boolean): `action=invalid`
* `failed` (any other finished status): `action=failed`, unless the reviewed SHA is not the branch tip
* `clear`: continue to the security review
* `open`: findings remain

A null or `skipped` security status means that review did not run.
A security review of a different commit is ignored.
A pending security review skips.
An open security review keeps the loop open.

On a Renovate pull request, once both reviews are finished,
the job waits up to two minutes (eight times, 15 seconds apart)
for Dependency Review to go idle on the branch.
If a run is still active, the action is `skip`:
that run's completion starts this workflow again.
The loop also skips when the latest completed Dependency Review run
is missing, not a success, or not still a commit on the pull request.
A failed run does not fall back to an older success.

The round counts distinct commits on the pull request
that `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` has reviewed, up to the reviewed commit.
Only that app's reviews and its own issue comments count
(the summary `code_review.commit_sha`, a review `commit_id`,
and a "Reviewed commit" receipt).
On a Renovate pull request, every reviewed commit at or before the Dependency Review baseline
is round 1.
Each later reviewed commit is another round.
The cap is 3.

When findings are open and every open Codex thread already asks for a decision
(the last comment is from Claude and contains **NEEDS HUMAN**),
the action is `skip`.
More than 100 threads is treated as still open, not as waiting.
Otherwise the action is `cap` at round 3 or more, and `fix` below that.
`done` is a clear code review whose security review is absent or clear,
and the reviewed SHA is still the branch tip.

A state line that is not the expected JSON yields `invalid`.

===== report

Display name: Stop the loop.
Needs `route`.
Runs for `done`, `cap`, `failed`, and `invalid`.
No timeout.

If the branch tip is no longer the reviewed SHA, the job exits without commenting.

* `done`: comment that Codex has no unresolved findings and the loop is finished.
* `cap`: comment that findings remain after that many reviews, add **NEEDS HUMAN**,
  and add `help wanted`.
* `failed`: comment the status and the summary URL, add **NEEDS HUMAN**, and add `help wanted`.
  The restart is a new push or a review request in a comment.
  The `claude-review` label does not change this summary.
* `invalid`: comment that the state line could not be read, add **NEEDS HUMAN**,
  and add `help wanted`.

===== fix

Display name: Address the Codex findings.
Needs `route`.
Runs for `action=fix`.
Timeout 60 minutes.

. Check out the pull request branch, `fetch-depth: 0`, `persist-credentials: false`.
  The job token is not written into `.git/config`.
. Stop when `HEAD` is not the reviewed SHA.
  A later review handles the new tip.
. Set up Node `26.x`.
. `npm ci`, or `npm install` when `npm ci` fails.
  Both failing leaves the commit tools off and continues.
. Restore `.claude` and `.mcp.json` from the default branch after install,
  so the pull request checkout cannot change Claude's project settings.
. Build the task text.
  A dependency pull request must not repeat the Dependency Review report.
  It follows the `update-dependency` skill for any dependency or configuration change.
  An issue pull request takes its scope from that issue's body and from maintainer comments.
  The pull request body is not the task.
  Other people's issue and comment text is untrusted.
. Run Claude in agent mode (`prompt` on a comment event).
  `CLAUDE_BRANCH` tells the signed-commit tool which branch to use.
  `allowed_bots` is `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot],renovate[bot]`.
  `restrict_untrusted_prs` is `false`.
  `use_commit_signing` is `true`.
  The prompt tells Claude to read review comments and review bodies,
  never to rewrite history,
  and never to edit `.github/`, `.claude/`, or `.mcp.json`.
  A finding already fixed at the reviewed commit gets a reply and no code change.
  If every finding is already fixed, Claude does not commit.
  A finding that needs a decision gets **NEEDS HUMAN**, `help wanted`, and no commit.
  Otherwise Claude pushes one commit and replies on each thread it fixed,
  including the full commit SHA.
  Claude does not resolve threads and does not post a Codex mention.
. Fail the job when the action did not run Claude.
  The job comments, adds `help wanted`, and exits non-zero.
. Read the branch tip through the API.
  A commit counts only when it is ahead of the reviewed SHA.
. Resolve threads whose last reply is from Claude,
  contains the new SHA or the reviewed SHA,
  and does not contain **NEEDS HUMAN**.
  The step is `continue-on-error: true`.
  At most 100 threads are read.
. When Claude did not push:
  stay quiet if every open Codex thread already asks for a decision;
  comment that the loop is finished when none remain open and this run resolved some;
  otherwise comment **NEEDS HUMAN** and add `help wanted`.

Allowed tools:

* `Read`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `mcp__github_file_ops__commit_files`
* `Bash(npm install)`, `Bash(npm outdated)`, `Bash(npm ls:*)`, `Bash(npm view:*)`
* `Bash(npm run lint)`, `Bash(npm run lint:build)`, `Bash(npm run dist)`
* `Bash(git status)`, `Bash(git log:*)`, `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git show:*)`
* `Bash(gh issue view:*)`, `Bash(gh pr view:*)`, `Bash(gh pr diff:*)`, `Bash(gh pr list:*)`
* `Bash(gh pr comment:*)`
* `Bash(gh pr edit * --add-label *)`, `Bash(gh pr edit * --remove-label *)`
* `Bash(gh release list:*)`, `Bash(gh release view:*)`
* `Bash(gh api repos/*/pulls/*/comments*)`, `Bash(gh api repos/*/pulls/*/reviews*)`
* `Bash(gh api repos/*/compare/*)`, `Bash(gh api repos/*/releases*)`, `Bash(gh api repos/*/contents/*)`
* `WebFetch` for `github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `www.npmjs.com`,
  `www.typescriptlang.org`, `babeljs.io`, `gulpjs.com`, `prettier.io`, and `jestjs.io`

Disallowed tools: `git merge`, `git rebase`, `git pull`, `git commit`, and `git push`.
On an install failure the commit-file and delete-file tools are disallowed as well.

==== Place in the flow

Codex posts and edits one summary comment per pull request.
This workflow is the response.
It does not request a review.
Publish pull requests are not in the loop.
After three rounds the workflow only reports the findings.
To start the loop again on a Renovate pull request, add `claude-review`
so Dependency Review runs and, on success, this workflow reads the summary again.
After a failed Codex review, the summary stays until Codex reviews a new push
or a person requests a review.
Drafts are not reviewed.

=== codex-watchdog.yaml

==== Name

Codex Review Watchdog.

==== Triggers

* `schedule`: cron `0 * * * *` (hourly)
* `workflow_dispatch`

No label filter and no mention condition.

==== Permissions

Job `watch`:

* `contents: read` to read the head commit time
* `pull-requests: write` to comment
* `issues: write` for the `help wanted` label

==== Secrets

None.
The step uses `github.token` only.
It does not post the Codex review trigger comment.

==== Node.js

This workflow does not set up Node.js.

==== Actions

None.
The step is shell and `gh`.

==== Concurrency

Group `codex-watchdog`, `cancel-in-progress: true`.
No `queue` setting.

==== Jobs

===== watch

Display name: Flag pull requests Codex has not reviewed.
Timeout 15 minutes.
Runs in `runner.temp`.

The job lists open pull requests whose head repository is this one,
and keeps:

* author `renovate[bot]`, or
* author `claude[bot]` and branch `claude-issue-<number>-`.

A head whose committer date is less than two hours old is left alone.
A head counts as reviewed when `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` has a review on that SHA,
or an issue comment from that app that contains the full SHA
or a "Reviewed commit" receipt of its first ten hex characters.

Only comments from `github-actions[bot]` that contain `perfective-codex-watchdog` count as this job's markers.
Another person's comment cannot silence the flag.

* No review, and this SHA is not already flagged:
  comment **NEEDS HUMAN**, mention that drafts are not reviewed,
  and add `help wanted`.
  One comment per head.
  A later commit can be flagged again.
  Removing the label does not bring it back for the same head.
* A review exists and the latest marker is a flag:
  comment that the flag is cleared.
  Remove `help wanted` only when the latest `labeled` event for that label
  is `github-actions[bot]` and is after the flag.
  A label from Dependency Review, Claude, or a person stays.

==== Place in the flow

This is the backstop for the Codex loop.
It does not start Claude and it does not ask Codex to review.
`schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` run from the default branch.

=== publish-pr.yaml

==== Name

Publish PR.

==== Triggers

* `issues`: `labeled`
* `issue_comment`: `created`
* `pull_request_review_comment`: `created`
* `pull_request_review`: `submitted`

Workflow `permissions` are `{}`.

The `prepare` job runs when either:

* the event is `issues`, the label is `claude`, the issue is open,
  and the title starts with `Release @perfective/build v`, or
* the event is a comment or review on a Publish pull request,
  the text contains a Claude mention,
  and the author is a maintainer.

An issue comment has no head ref, so a title that starts with `Publish v` selects it.
The step then checks that the branch is `publish-vX.Y.Z` in this repository.
A review event checks that head ref directly.

A release issue can sit until the label is added.
Nothing in this workflow runs on issue creation alone.
The general Claude workflow does not run on this issue or on this pull request.

==== Permissions

Job `prepare`:

* `contents: read`
* `issues: read`
* `pull-requests: read`

Job `publish-pr`:

* `contents: write` to push the Publish branch
* `pull-requests: write` to open, update, and comment
* `issues: write` to report a failure
* `id-token: write` for the Claude GitHub App token
* `actions: read` to read Continuous Integration
* `checks: read` for `gh pr checks`

==== Secrets

`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.

==== Node.js

Job `publish-pr` uses `26.x` via `actions/setup-node@v7`.
`prepare` does not install Node.

==== Actions

`actions/checkout@v7` and `actions/setup-node@v7` on `publish-pr`.
`anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` on `publish-pr`.
`prepare` is shell and `gh`.

==== Concurrency

Job `publish-pr` uses group `publish-pr-<version>`,
`cancel-in-progress: false`, and `queue: max`.
`prepare` has no concurrency group.

==== Jobs

===== prepare

Display name: Find the release.
Timeout 5 minutes.

The version is `X.Y.Z` or `X.Y.Z-<prerelease>` from the issue title,
or from a `publish-v` branch name on a pull request.
The branch is `publish-v<version>`.

The job fails when:

* the title or branch does not match
* the pull request is not a branch in this repository, or is not open
* the `v<version>` tag already exists
* a Publish pull request from that branch is already merged

When the branch already exists, `resume` is `true`
and `pr` is the open pull request number, if one is open.
A mention on a missing branch fails.
A label on the issue does not fail when the branch is missing:
the first commit creates it from `main`.

Outputs: `version`, `branch`, `issue`, `pr`, `resume`.

===== publish-pr

Display name: Open or fix the Publish PR.
Needs `prepare`.
Timeout 30 minutes.
`CLAUDE_BRANCH` is the Publish branch.

. Check out with `fetch-depth: 0` (history and tags).
  When resuming, check out the existing Publish branch.
  Otherwise check out the default branch.
. Set up Node `26.x`.
. `npm ci`.
  There is no `npm install` fallback.
. When `package.json` is not already this version,
  run `npm version <version> --no-git-tag-version` and `npm update`.
  Record whether that bump happened, and the latest tag (`git describe --tags --abbrev=0`).
. Describe the run for the prompt:
  whether the version was just bumped,
  whether the branch is new or continued,
  and, for a comment or review, the maintainer's request.
. Run Claude in agent mode.
  `use_commit_signing` is `true`.
  `restrict_untrusted_prs` is `false`.
  `allow_fork_prs` is `false`.
  `additional_permissions` repeats `actions: read` and `checks: read`.
  A new branch: write the changelog section, sync `README.adoc` and `README.md`
  (including peer ranges) from `ROADMAP.adoc` gaps the commits address,
  update `ROADMAP.adoc`, run `npm run lint`, `npm run lint:build`, and `npm run dist`,
  commit `Publish vX.Y.Z` with only `package.json`, `package-lock.json`,
  `CHANGELOG.adoc`, `README.adoc`, `README.md`, and `ROADMAP.adoc`,
  and open the pull request against `main` with `Closes #<issue>` when an issue is open.
  The body ends with the italic line `*Written by Claude*`.
  An existing branch: fix only those files
  (plus the package files when this run bumped them).
  A fix that needs any other file is **NEEDS HUMAN** and is not committed.
  Commit a new fix commit, or commit nothing.
  Open the pull request if none is open.
  Otherwise update the body when the changelog changed, and comment with the full SHA.
  The prompt tells Claude not to write a Claude mention in the pull request body or in a comment.
  Claude does not tag, release, or publish.
. If no open Publish pull request from that branch exists, comment on the issue or the source pull request
  and fail the job.
  The retry is to remove and re-add the `claude` label.
  An existing branch is continued, not deleted.

Allowed tools:

* `Read`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `mcp__github_file_ops__commit_files`
* `Bash(npm run lint)`, `Bash(npm run lint:build)`, `Bash(npm run dist)`
* `Bash(npm ls:*)`, `Bash(npm view:*)`
* `Bash(git status)`, `Bash(git log:*)`, `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git show:*)`
* `Bash(gh issue view:*)`, `Bash(gh pr view:*)`, `Bash(gh pr checks:*)`
* `Bash(gh run list:*)`, `Bash(gh run view:*)`
* `Bash(gh pr create:*)`
* `Bash(gh pr edit * --body-file *)`, `Bash(gh pr comment * --body-file *)`

Disallowed tools:

* `mcp__github_file_ops__delete_files`
* `npm install`, `npm update`, `npm version`, and `npm publish`
* `git commit`, `git push`, `git merge`, `git rebase`, `git pull`, and `git tag`
* `gh release` and `gh pr merge`

The same allow-list is used for the first run, a re-added label, and a Claude mention on the pull request.

==== Place in the flow

This is the only workflow that opens the Publish pull request.
Continuous Integration then runs on that pull request.
The maintainer reviews it.
Codex Review does not.
After the squash-merge, the maintainer signs and pushes the tag,
and `publish.yaml` publishes.

=== publish.yaml

==== Name

Publish.

==== Triggers

`push` of tags matching `v*`.

Workflow `permissions` are `{}`.
npm trusted publishing is bound to this file name.
Renaming the file breaks publishing.

==== Permissions

Job `verify`: `contents: read`.

Job `npm`:

* `id-token: write` for npm trusted publishing and provenance
* `contents: read`

==== Secrets

None.
npm uses the job's OIDC token.

==== Node.js

Job `npm` uses `26.x` via `actions/setup-node@v7`,
with `registry-url` `https://registry.npmjs.org`.
`verify` does not install Node.
It reads the tag and `package.json` through the GitHub API.

==== Actions

`actions/checkout@v7` and `actions/setup-node@v7` on `npm`.
`verify` is shell and `gh`.
Checkout is not used to verify the tag:
`actions/checkout` does not keep the annotated tag object,
and GitHub's API reports the signature verification.

==== Concurrency

Workflow group `publish-<git ref>`, `cancel-in-progress: false`.
No `queue` setting (this concurrency block is on the workflow).

==== Jobs

===== verify

Display name: Verify the tag.
Timeout 5 minutes.

The tag must match `vX.Y.Z` or `vX.Y.Z-<prerelease>`.
The job fails when:

* the tag is lightweight (the git object is not a tag)
* GitHub does not verify the signature
* the tag does not point at a commit
* that commit is not on `main` or on `v<major>.<minor>.x`
  (`compare` status `identical` or `behind`)
* `package.json` at that commit has a different `version`
* `CHANGELOG.adoc` at that commit has no `== vX.Y.Z` section,
  or the section is empty

The npm dist-tag is:

* `latest` for a non-prerelease tag whose commit is on `main`
* `backport-<major>.<minor>` for a non-prerelease tag whose commit is on the backport branch
  (not a semver range)
* `next` when the version contains a hyphen (a prerelease), on either branch

Outputs: `sha`, `version`, `dist_tag`.

===== npm

Display name: Publish NPM package.
Needs `verify`.
Timeout 15 minutes.

. Check out the verified commit.
. Set up Node `26.x` with the npm registry.
. `npm ci`.
. `npm run lint:build`.
. `npm run dist`.
. Publish `./dist` with `npm publish --provenance --tag <dist-tag>`
  when `npm view <name>@<version>` does not already succeed.
  A rerun of a version that is already on npm exits successfully without publishing.

The job does not create a GitHub Release.

==== Place in the flow

This is the last automated step.
It runs only from the signed tag push.
The maintainer creates the GitHub Release for that tag after it.
Prerelease tags stay on the `next` dist-tag until a 1.0 line needs them.

== Related configuration

The workflows assume this configuration.
It is not itself a workflow.

=== Renovate

`renovate.json` extends `config:recommended` and `security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm`.
It ignores `group:monorepos` and `group:recommended`.
`automerge` is false.
`rangeStrategy` is `bump`.
The Dependency Dashboard is on.
`prConcurrentLimit` is 3 and `prHourlyLimit` is 2.
`rebaseLabel` is `renovate-regenerate`.
OSV vulnerability alerts are on.
Pull requests are labeled `dependencies`;
vulnerability alerts also get `vulnerability`.
Major updates, peer dependency updates, and `typescript` updates also get `help wanted`.
GitHub Actions updates use `schedule:weekly`.

There is no Dependabot config and no `CODEOWNERS` file.

=== Agent entry points

* `AGENTS.md` is the maintainer guide the prompts tell Claude to follow.
* `.agents/skills/` holds `update-dependency`, `update-dependencies`, and `prepare-release`.
  `.claude/skills` is a symlink to that directory.
* `.cursor/rules/commit-changes.mdc` and `.cursor/rules/pr-review.mdc`
  are Cursor rules.
  The workflows do not read them.
* `specs/renovate.adoc` is the end-state design for dependency review.
  The workflows in this file are the path that runs today.

=== What the prompts refuse to edit

Dependency Review's skill, and the Codex Review fix prompt,
tell Claude not to edit `.github/`, `.claude/`, or `.mcp.json` on those runs.
There is no `.mcp.json` in this repository today.
Publish PR may edit only the Publish file list in its prompt.
